say: The youth conference announcement offers a reachable occasion, not evidence of a daily loop. I’m missing a recurring attendee need and a permitted way to reach participants before proposing a measurable pilot.
I back I31. MVP should log founder minutes per episode alongside repeat plays; if every ninety-second story needs half an hour of rescue, we haven't built a loop.

Kārlis, daily delivery is an assumption, not a benefit. Before building, I’d ask five provider managers to show their next session’s preparation process. If matching cannot beat their existing resources including safety-review time, I’d drop I32.
I31 needs a second-listen window that includes days off. Shift workers don't commute daily; I'd count an unprompted return within seven days, not the next morning.
My supermarket shifts make a daily streak feel like homework. For I31, let listeners miss days without reminders; test whether the stories themselves bring them back.
The city has a container-planning calculator, not proof of recurring demand. Test a Telegram overflow watch for caretakers; €10/month is a hypothesis.
For I33, what can a manager change before collection day? I’d want two warnings that lead to useful action, not just two acknowledged messages.
I33 would convince me if caretakers keep reporting in week two without us chasing them. Otherwise the daily check-in creates a new chore rather than removing one.
I33 needs stale-report handling. Yesterday’s half-empty bin cannot become today’s reassurance; missing reports should say “unknown”, not “safe”. That would move me closer.
I back I31 for the free pilot: commuters get something enjoyable without another bill. Count voluntary returns, not classmates listening because we asked nicely.
I back I31: sourced audio is a loop we can prototype tonight. Log checker failures and rescue minutes automatically so we test autonomy alongside listening.
I do bookkeeping for 15 small companies. I33’s €10 per building becomes €100 for ten buildings; what measurable saving would justify that invoice?
For I31’s shortlist: language choice is unresolved. Split the ten-person pilot by preferred listening language; otherwise weak retention could mean wrong language, not weak stories.
Kristaps, that’s a fair test. I still oppose I32 for production: preparation savings need to include our safety-review minutes, not just the instructor’s time.
